There may be a couple factors at play, in isolation or working together.

  1. If you have a naval base, you can concentrate Anti-aircraft guns around it to defend it, you can also put fighters in the air to cover it. The ships themselves may also be able to get in the fight with their anti-aircraft guns. There are a finite number of naval bases so you can easily allocate forces to defend them. Cities on the other hand are more numerous and spread out. You would not be able to put a large number of guns in every city because there are so many that need to be protected. As a consequence cities would be a softer target.

  2. Ships do not spend all their time in base, they could be out patrolling, training or running missions against the Germans. You might only be able to target a small fraction of the navy at any given time.

  3. By attacking the cities you damage the morale of the populace, potentially raising support for a move to seek peace.

  4. Industry would be concentrated in cities, by attacking them you undermine the ability to maintain the war effort.
